Run MAGPlot's QC on one delivery

Source: R/magp_run.R
magp_run_qc.Rd

Runs MAGPlot 2.0's quality checks on one delivery from start to finish: pre-flight, the checks of Layers 0 to 4, each issue's provider key and class, the run's files in <output_dir>/<run_id>/, and, by default, a report and an issues CSV for each contributor.

Usage

magp_run_qc(
  tables,
  output_dir,
  overrides = NULL,
  lineage = NULL,
  pipeline_fill = NULL,
  report = TRUE,
  settings = list()
)

Arguments

tables

One delivery's tables: magp_read_delivery()'s result, the path of the delivery's .Rdata file, which the run passes to magp_read_delivery(), or a named list of data.frames, one per table. More than one path, or a list holding CSV paths, is refused; check CSV files with gpq_check_conformance().

output_dir

The folder that holds run folders, made if it doesn't exist. The run writes into <output_dir>/<run_id>/.

overrides

NULL, or your overrides of issue classes: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file, as gpq_classify_issues() takes them, whose scope may also name the issues' group columns: the run's magp_contributor_id, jurisdiction and magp_dataset_id, and the plot's key magp_plot_id.

lineage

NULL, or the provider's raw values of the cells the pipeline changed: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file with the columns table_name, record_pk, column_name, raw_value and raw_source. The classes read it as evidence, and each contributor's report shows a listed cell's raw value beside its issue among the issues to act on, where the record's key is given and, written as text, matches no other record's in its table, as gpq_build_reports() does.

pipeline_fill

NULL, or the cells the pipeline's missing-value fill wrote: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file with the columns table_name, record_pk, column_name and written_value, which the classes read as their evidence filled.

report

TRUE to build each contributor's report and issues CSV; FALSE writes the results and run metadata, with no contributor reports or issues CSVs.

settings

A named list of settings, which come before the rule set's, the options' and the built-in values (see groundplotqc_options).

Value

The run's results, invisibly: a gpq_results object as gpq_check_conformance() describes it, each issue with its provider key and class, as written to the run folder. A run that pre-flight stops returns nothing.

Details

The run makes its run ID, then loads the tables, then runs pre-flight, so a run that pre-flight stops still records the contributors its tables hold. This is the reverse of gpq_check_conformance(), which runs pre-flight before it reads any table. Pre-flight checks MAGPlot's specification, rule set, report text and settings, and its warning reaches you, naming the run's reports/preflight.html. When it stops, the run writes metadata/run.csv, with the outcome stopped_preflight, and metadata/spec_manifest.csv, as well as pre-flight's two files, metadata/preflight.csv and reports/preflight.html, then stops with an error of class gpq_preflight_error.

Otherwise the run checks Layers 0 to 4, with MAGPlot's group columns magp_contributor_id, jurisdiction and magp_dataset_id and its problem unit, the plot (magp_plot_id of magp_plots). It then gives each issue its provider key, from its contributor's lineage spec and Ontario's age-tree flag, and its class, from your overrides first, then from the evidence: the columns MAGPlot's pipeline computes, pipeline_fill, and lineage together with MAGPlot's translation tables' provider codes. It writes the results and the run metadata, and with report = TRUE builds the reports.

Pre-flight checks overrides, lineage and pipeline_fill, and the run then reads them as gpq_classify_issues() reads them, before any check. The run stops there wherever gpq_classify_issues() would on an input that pre-flight lets pass, such as an overrides column that is an attribute of the specification but not one of the issues' group columns, or a cell that lineage or pipeline_fill lists twice.

In metadata/run.csv, run_start is when the run started and run_end is set just before the results are written: the time between them covers loading the tables, pre-flight, the checks, the provider keys and the classes, not the writing or the reports.

In metadata/inputs.csv, each table's row (tables:<name>) names the delivery's .Rdata file and its SHA-256, with the table's row count as its detail. A delivery that holds magp_meta adds a row with the input magp_meta, naming the same file and hash; magp_meta itself is never checked. These rows name the file and its hash even for a table you added to magp_read_delivery()'s result, replaced in it or edited in it before the run, so they don't show which tables you changed. Tables given as a plain named list are recorded as "in memory", with no hash. Each run input that classification is given adds a row after these, with the input overrides, filled (your pipeline_fill), lineage, computed or crosswalk and the rows classification reads from it as its detail. A CSV file you gave is recorded by its file name and SHA-256; a data.frame is recorded as "in memory", with no hash, and so are MAGPlot's own computed and crosswalk, which every run has.

The run lets go of the tables once each issue has its provider key, before the classes and the reports. Their memory is freed only when nothing else holds them, so give the .Rdata file's path to use the least memory.

settings goes to pre-flight, the checks and the classes; its lang, row_cap, example_cap and cell_cap also go to the reports.

A stop after pre-flight passes and before the results are written leaves pre-flight's two files and no metadata/run.csv. A stop while the reports are built leaves the run's saved results, whose reports gpq_build_reports() builds again.

See also

magp_read_delivery(), which loads a delivery; gpq_build_reports(), which builds a saved run's reports again.

Examples

# magp_example's tables saved as a delivery saves them, each as its own object.
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rdata")
save(list = names(magp_example), envir = list2env(magp_example), file = path)
output <- tempfile("runs")
# MAGPlot's bundled specification has known pre-flight warnings, so this warning is expected.
results <- magp_run_qc(path, output)
#> Warning: Pre-flight found 32 warning(s); see /tmp/RtmpL0xf7E/runs1e66a8bbe0f/20261103T175534Z_9be761/reports/preflight.html.
run_dir <- file.path(output, results$metadata$run$run_id)
list.files(run_dir, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "metadata/clashes.csv"       "metadata/inputs.csv"       
#>  [3] "metadata/preflight.csv"     "metadata/rules.csv"        
#>  [5] "metadata/run.csv"           "metadata/self_test.csv"    
#>  [7] "metadata/settings.csv"      "metadata/spec_manifest.csv"
#>  [9] "reports/100.html"           "reports/110.html"          
#> [11] "reports/preflight.html"     "tables/100_issues.csv"     
#> [13] "tables/110_issues.csv"      "tables/corrections.csv"    
#> [15] "tables/issues.csv"          "tables/results.csv"
